content: The Indiana School for the Deaf (ISD) is a fully accredited educational institution dedicated to serving Deaf and hard-of-hearing students. It is located in Indianapolis, Indiana. History The first school for the Deaf in Indiana was not originally called the Indiana School for the Deaf. It was named the Willard School, after its founder, William Willard. William Willard, a Deaf educator, had previously taught at the Ohio School for the Deaf in Columbus, Ohio. In May 1843, he traveled to Indianapolis to propose the establishment of a school for the Deaf. After gaining the support of the General Assembly, he recruited approximately twelve students. Both he and his wife, Eliza, served as teachers at the school. Over time, the school expanded, and in 1846, a law was passed officially establishing the Willard School as the sixth state school for the Deaf in the United States. It was also the first Deaf school to provide free education to Deaf and hard-of-hearing students. The school relocated several times before settling on an 80-acre property on East 42nd Street. At this point, the name was changed to the Indiana School for the Deaf. The main buildings on the current campus are recognized as historic landmarks. Philosophy The school follows a Bilingual/Bicultural philosophy, which emphasizes language acquisition and proficiency in both American Sign Language (ASL) and English. By fostering an enriched academic and cultural learning environment, ISD helps its Deaf and hard-of-hearing students develop a strong sense of identity within the Deaf community. Additionally, students acquire the knowledge, skills, and attitudes necessary to interact effectively with members of a multicultural and diverse society. Academics ISD offers a range of programs for students from infancy through high school. These programs include: Parent Infant Program: This program works closely with parents and their Deaf or hard-of-hearing children from birth to age three. Children can officially enroll as students at ISD starting at 18 months of age. Preschool: This program serves children up to Pre-Kindergarten. Elementary School: This program provides academics and activities for students in Kindergarten through 5th grade. Middle School: This program serves students in grades 6 through 8. High School: This program serves students in grades 9 through 12. Residency ISD is also a residential school, offering dormitory accommodations for students who live too far to commute daily. Students arrive on Sundays and depart on Fridays. Separate dormitories are available for male and female students, and they are organized by age group: Preschool, Elementary, Middle School, and High School. The residential program provides opportunities for extracurricular activities, peer interaction, personal growth and development, and academic achievement. Athletics ISD offers a variety of athletic programs for students in grades 5 through 12. Sports are available for both male and female students.
